title: Show the open-ticket count on the Open tab
body: Adds a live count next to the Open folder so agents can see the size of the queue at a glance. Display only.
truth: Nothing is wrong with this change. It is here because a reviewer who always finds something has found nothing.
reactNote: A two-line change. The diff is all you need, and it is all you have.
sygnalNote: A calm report here is only worth something next to its "did not look at" list: it does not read the view's markup.

title: Show a priority badge on each ticket
body: Renders `ticket.priority` as a small badge in the ticket list, so high-priority tickets stand out. No change to how tickets are handled.
kind: A new request nobody asked for
truth: Selecting a ticket now posts its customer's email address to a third-party metrics host. The description does not mention it.
breaks: selecting a ticket sends nothing over the network
reactNote: The call is in the diff, in two files the description does not mention. A lint rule or CODEOWNERS on api.js would ask someone to look. Nothing tells you what triggers it or that it wasn't in the description.
sygnalNote: The new host is the first line of the report, tied to the click that fires it, whatever the description says.

title: Refactor: extract the ticket actions into their own module
body: The detail logic was getting long. Moves send/close into their own module and folds the repeated request code into one helper. No behaviour change.
kind: A guard lost in a refactor
truth: The check that refuses to close a ticket with an unsent reply did not survive the move. Closing now discards the reply silently.
breaks: refuses to close a ticket with an unsent reply
reactNote: The defect is a line that is absent from the + side of a move. You find it by comparing old and new by eye.
sygnalNote: The guard is named. The report also raises two false alarms: the requests are now built in a helper, so it calls them new. It is noisier on refactors than the other changes suggest.

title: Clear the search when you switch folders
body: Stale search text hid tickets after a folder switch. Switching folders now resets the view.
kind: A state write that reaches another feature
truth: "Reset the view" also clears `drafts`, so every unsent reply on every ticket disappears when someone switches folders.
breaks: keeps an unsent reply when you switch folders and come back
reactNote: setDrafts({}) is in the diff. Knowing it matters means knowing who else reads drafts, which the diff does not show.
sygnalNote: The report names the extra keys and which component reads them. It cannot say that clearing drafts is wrong, only that this action reaches them now.

title: Reject whitespace-only replies, spell out the send rule
body: Names the two conditions in `canSend` so the rule reads clearly.
kind: A logic slip in a helper (the limit of the tool)
truth: `!(blank && closed)` should be `!(blank || closed)`. Blank replies can now be sent, and so can replies on closed tickets. The file is byte-for-byte the same in both apps, and Sygnal's tooling can only say that something in the helper differs.
breaks: does not send a blank reply
reactNote: Same file, same diff, same reading. Your eyes or a test.
sygnalNote: "Helper changed" points you at the file. It adds nothing about the logic. A property test, a replay or a human has to catch this one, in either framework.
